text: Which lawyers in Adelaide are best for TPD and superannuation insurance claims?

result.keyword: Which lawyers in Adelaide are best for TPD and superannuation insurance claims?
result.markdown:
Yes. I searched specifically for Adelaide/South Australian lawyers who handle **TPD (Total and Permanent Disability), superannuation insurance, income protection and disputed/declined claims**. Based on specialist focus, the lawyers’ experience and the available client feedback, I’d shortlist these:

### My Adelaide shortlist

| Firm | Why I’d consider them | Best suited to |
|---|---|---|
| **DBH Lawyers** | **Very strong specialist option.** Partner Hayley Gagin has focused exclusively on TPD since 2017 and leads DBH's TPD team. The firm says the team specialises in superannuation insurance law and prepares claims carefully before submission. [dbh.com.au](https://dbh.com.au/team/hayley-gagin/?utm_source=chatgpt.com) | TPD claims where you want a **dedicated Adelaide TPD team** |
| **Berrill & Watson** | **One of my top picks for a difficult/complex claim.** They specialise in superannuation and insurance rather than general personal injury. Principal Tom Cobban has 15+ years working exclusively in this area and represents insured people, not insurers. They also specifically service SA. [www.berrillwatson.com.au](https://www.berrillwatson.com.au/people/tom-cobban/?utm_source=chatgpt.com) | **Declined TPD, complex insurance disputes, multiple policies, insurer resistance** |
| **Tindall Gask Bentley (TGB)** | Established Adelaide firm with a dedicated TPD/superannuation practice. Their lawyers handle TPD/super claims and they say they've helped thousands of South Australians with TPD claims. [tgb.com.au](https://tgb.com.au/superannuation-tpd-claims-adelaide-south-australia/?utm_source=chatgpt.com) | TPD claims where you want a **large, established SA practice** |
| **Andersons Solicitors** | Highly regarded Adelaide personal-injury firm and worth comparing if your TPD claim is connected to another compensation matter. | TPD alongside **workers' compensation/personal injury** |
| **WKB TPD Lawyers - TPD Claim Lawyers** | Particularly interesting because the practice is explicitly branded around TPD rather than general law. | Straightforward **TPD/super insurance claims** |
| **PMN Personal Injury Lawyers Adelaide** | Strong local personal-injury practice with good current business-review numbers; worth getting a second opinion from if the matter overlaps with personal injury. | TPD + **broader personal injury** |


### If it were my claim

I'd probably get **three initial opinions**:

**1. DBH Lawyers** — particularly because Hayley Gagin's practice is unusually focused on TPD. She has been concentrating on TPD claims since 2017 and leads the firm's dedicated TPD team. [dbh.com.au](https://dbh.com.au/team/hayley-gagin/?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

**2. Berrill & Watson** — my pick to add if there's any complication: a previous rejection, an insurer disputing medical evidence, multiple super funds, an old policy, or a potentially large claim. Tom Cobban has spent his career in superannuation/insurance claims and has acted against the major insurers. [www.berrillwatson.com.au](https://www.berrillwatson.com.au/people/tom-cobban/?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

**3. TGB** — a good Adelaide-based alternative with substantial local experience in TPD/superannuation claims. [tgb.com.au](https://tgb.com.au/superannuation-tpd-claims-adelaide-south-australia/?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

Berrill & Watson's published client feedback is also unusually relevant: recent reviews specifically discuss **TPD and superannuation claims**, with clients describing the team's communication, guidance and handling of complex insurer issues positively. [www.berrillwatson.com.au](https://www.berrillwatson.com.au/people/tom-cobban/?utm_source=chatgpt.com)[tgb.com.au](https://tgb.com.au/superannuation-tpd-claims-adelaide-south-australia/?utm_source=chatgpt.com)[www.berrillwatson.com.au](https://www.berrillwatson.com.au/about/what-our-clients-say/?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

### What about the big national firms?

**Slater and Gordon** is certainly legitimate and has a dedicated national superannuation/TPD practice covering TPD, income protection, terminal illness and insurance litigation. It advertises no-win-no-fee representation. [www.slatergordon.com.au](https://www.slatergordon.com.au/superannuation-and-insurance/total-and-permanent-disability-tpd-claims?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

I'd nevertheless put **DBH, Berrill & Watson and TGB ahead of it for an Adelaide TPD claim** if the objective is to find a specialist rather than simply a large national firm.

One reason is that TPD claims can turn heavily on the **exact wording of the policy, your occupation, medical evidence and the applicable definition of disability**. Having someone who does these claims regularly can make a meaningful difference.

**Important:** "best" depends substantially on whether you're making a fresh claim or fighting a rejection. If you tell me **(1) whether your TPD claim has been rejected, (2) roughly how much the insurance benefit is, and (3) whether it's through your super fund**, I can narrow this to the **2–3 Adelaide lawyers I'd contact first**, including their fee/no-win-no-fee arrangements and recent reviews.

Yes. I searched specifically for Adelaide/South Australian lawyers who handle **TPD (Total and Permanent Disability), superannuation insurance, income protection and disputed/declined claims**. Based on specialist focus, the lawyers’ experience and the available client feedback, I’d shortlist these:

| Firm | Why I’d consider them | Best suited to |
|---|---|---|
| **DBH Lawyers** | **Very strong specialist option.** Partner Hayley Gagin has focused exclusively on TPD since 2017 and leads DBH's TPD team. The firm says the team specialises in superannuation insurance law and prepares claims carefully before submission. items.markdown:
### If it were my claim

I'd probably get **three initial opinions**:

**1. DBH Lawyers** — particularly because Hayley Gagin's practice is unusually focused on TPD. She has been concentrating on TPD claims since 2017 and leads the firm's dedicated TPD team. [dbh.com.au](https://dbh.com.au/team/hayley-gagin/?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

**2. Berrill & Watson** — my pick to add if there's any complication: a previous rejection, an insurer disputing medical evidence, multiple super funds, an old policy, or a potentially large claim. Tom Cobban has spent his career in superannuation/insurance claims and has acted against the major insurers. [www.berrillwatson.com.au](https://www.berrillwatson.com.au/people/tom-cobban/?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

**3. TGB** — a good Adelaide-based alternative with substantial local experience in TPD/superannuation claims. [tgb.com.au](https://tgb.com.au/superannuation-tpd-claims-adelaide-south-australia/?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

Berrill & Watson's published client feedback is also unusually relevant: recent reviews specifically discuss **TPD and superannuation claims**, with clients describing the team's communication, guidance and handling of complex insurer issues positively. [www.berrillwatson.com.au](https://www.berrillwatson.com.au/people/tom-cobban/?utm_source=chatgpt.com)[tgb.com.au](https://tgb.com.au/superannuation-tpd-claims-adelaide-south-australia/?utm_source=chatgpt.com)[www.berrillwatson.com.au](https://www.berrillwatson.com.au/about/what-our-clients-say/?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

### What about the big national firms?

**Slater and Gordon** is certainly legitimate and has a dedicated national superannuation/TPD practice covering TPD, income protection, terminal illness and insurance litigation. It advertises no-win-no-fee representation. [www.slatergordon.com.au](https://www.slatergordon.com.au/superannuation-and-insurance/total-and-permanent-disability-tpd-claims?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

I'd nevertheless put **DBH, Berrill & Watson and TGB ahead of it for an Adelaide TPD claim** if the objective is to find a specialist rather than simply a large national firm.

One reason is that TPD claims can turn heavily on the **exact wording of the policy, your occupation, medical evidence and the applicable definition of disability**. Having someone who does these claims regularly can make a meaningful difference.

**Important:** "best" depends substantially on whether you're making a fresh claim or fighting a rejection. If you tell me **(1) whether your TPD claim has been rejected, (2) roughly how much the insurance benefit is, and (3) whether it's through your super fund**, I can narrow this to the **2–3 Adelaide lawyers I'd contact first**, including their fee/no-win-no-fee arrangements and recent reviews.
